title: A finding queued from a check still counts open
what: Moving a finding to a queue item marks it once, where every later check of that branch sees it: `relay queue add --from` given a check record writes the owner entry onto the review finding the check judged (the check names its review), or the check counts a finding queued when a queue item records it as its source. `relay check owner` accepts a check record the same way, or its refusal names the review to use.
why: 28 Oct, stub-guard change: the front queued finding F2 with `relay queue add --from <check record> F2`. The owner entry went into that check record only, so the next two checks, which judge from the review, still counted F2 open (`open 1, queued 0`). The front spent two extra fix-and-check cycles, about 1.5 h of wall time and 6 agents, before finding `relay check owner <review.json> F2` with `queue = slug`, which refuses a check record ("type must be review").
failing_case: Queue F2 of a check record with `relay queue add --from <check.json> F2`; run the next check of the branch against the review: F2 counts open.
pass_cases: After `relay queue add --from <check.json> F2`, the next check's mark shows queued 1, open 0.
`relay check owner <check.json> F2 --input` either works or names the review file in its refusal.

fact: Edited where: lib/relay_check.py does not exist; `relay check owner` is handled in bin/relay (grep, 28 Oct).
